answer: Cedar-interval arrival gating admits new identities only when their first actions land inside a randomized admission window whose timing is derived from a hidden committee seed. Each identity’s request inter-arrival distribution is then scored against that window shape, and identities that cluster at the nadir of expected traffic incur exponentially larger queue delays. An attacker must spread sybil registrations across many windows and mimic organic burstiness, forcing costly idle time and steady low-rate probing per fake identity rather than a single summit of cheap bulk signups.
